lead: Tesla / TSLA — the tariff reprieve the crowd is buying
smaller: Robinhood / HOOD — the bet the regulators are watching
Strategy / MSTR — Saylor buys again, the stock runs
PDD Holdings / PDD — the Temu parent that retail still likes
why_lead: Tesla closed at 278.39 after an 11.93% prior-session jump and a 16.97% five-session rally, still 15.77% below its 20-session reference of 330.53. The new dated catalyst is 24 March: Reuters on possible tariff leeway and Automotive News on auto tariffs being unlikely on April 2. Electrek's retail-investor framing and Yahoo's same-day explainer are the attention evidence.

Changed story, not the same essay: the Musk-dip theme led on 12, 17 and 24 March, and the 24 March lead rested on Musk's 21 March hang-on message. Today the catalyst is the tariff date and the reaction is a bounce that held and extended. The hang-on item is cut to context and no longer carries the lead.
Every citation rests on headlines dated before 00:00 UTC on 2025-03-25; no later outcome was used to choose the lead.
why_smaller: Robinhood: the 18 March lead's prediction-markets angle, kept as a shortened carryover because the changed story is the 24 March Massachusetts probe (Reuters exclusive), and the stock rose 9.02% in the session the probe was reported.

Strategy (MSTR): new to the retail section. Strategy's $584,000,000 bitcoin purchase (Daily Hodl, 24 March), the 16% jump on the dividend announcement (20 March) and the 10.43% session, against a bitcoin line that is flat over 20 sessions (+0.32%). Michael Saylor appeared on 6 March only as a reserve commentator in the bitcoin-reserve smaller.

PDD: new. A revenue miss (Business Insider and Investopedia, 20 March), analyst downgrades against retail optimism (Stocktwits, 24 March), and a 2X single-stock fund launched 12 March. Non-AI equity with no earlier appearance.
considered_not_chosen: Ripple / XRP: third XRP appearance in three weeks (lead on 3 and 20 March). The only new evidence is the fade to the 2.46 reference (-3.84% over five sessions) and a CoinShares ETP-inflow headline; a reversal too thin for a smaller slot against fresher evidence.

Quantum computing / IONQ: quantum has led on 7, 13, 19 and 21 March, and the 12 March smaller used the same "next revolution" hook. The 21 March director purchase and the 17.34% session do not change the story.

Oklo (OKLO): NRC pre-application readiness and board changes on 24 March, with a 13.81% session, but the attention evidence is company releases and one Barron's piece; nuclear was a smaller on 11 and 13 March.
Coinbase (COIN): trending-ticker list (Yahoo Finance UK, 24 March) and a Bernstein call (19 March), with no retail-flow evidence beyond the list.
Bloomberg, 23 March, on wild bets by Korean retail investors during the US tech rout: the feed gives the headline only and names no instrument, so no number can be attached to it.
Palantir (PLTR): +10.76% over five sessions, but its buyback catalyst was used on 21 March and the analyst pieces are not a new story.
Bitcoin miners (MARA +18.01% in the prior session; Riot's Rockdale deal on 24 March): IREN was the 21 March smaller on the same grid theme, and no retail-attention item for them appears in the feed.
Gold (GLD, -0.45% in the prior session): record-high headlines were used on 17, 19 and 24 March.
Aeva, Phunware, XTIA, Generac, DYDX and Prairie Operating: Stocktwits attention items, but none is on the market card, so no price can be cited.
Nvidia (NVDA): the Robinhood top-holding item is dated 14 March, and the roadmap-retail angle already ran as the 18 and 20 March smaller.
